bullets.title: Unstoppable: My Life So Far
bullets.creator: Maria Sharapova
bullets.note:
I got an early review copy of this after [our podcast
together](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/zlue04m77unhkog5k/opfkhq/aHR0cHM6Ly90aW0uYmxvZy8yMDE3LzA4LzI2L21hcmlhLXNoYXJhcG92YS8=),
and it’s absolutely fantastic thus far. It is co-authored by Rich Cohen, whose
books _The Fish That Ate the Whale_ and _The Sun & The Moon & The Rolling
Stones_ blew me away (Ryan Holiday and others are also huge fans). If you like
autobios and stories of persistence, this is definitely worth checking
out.**

bullets.title: one video that catches the eye
bullets.note:
After so many years outside
of Buenos Aires, I felt a longing to hear tango music, and di Sarli has always
been one of my favorites. This music is best listened to while dancing or
watching tango. Here is [one video that catches the
eye](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/zlue04m77unhkog5k/zvtghn/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g_dj1WbEhDUlV2OWp3WQ==),
and [here is another
video](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/zlue04m77unhkog5k/pnceh9/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g_dj1JU0twTC1PSHRpSQ==)
that is less exciting but arguably more subtle and nuanced. The song may seem
melancholic (as tango is often called), but I think it more accurately covers
the entire spectrum of human emotion, including the harder feelings we often
prefer to avoid.**
